[spoiler=[b]STARBOUND RP | Happiness of the Hawks[/b]][b]STARBOUND RP

Happiness of the Hawks

6 January 2167

ONC [i]Orange Creek[/i], Lagrange Point 4, Erene[/b]

There was a buzz, a soft hum of the Orange Creek's environmental systems that signaled the beginning of another simulated dawn. 

[list]"... Guess I'm still alive..."[/list]

Euphrasia emerged from the compact sleeping pod, feeling more exhausted than she's ever been. "Another dull day", she'd mouth after blinking for three seconds to reorient herself to the bright lights of her low-ceilinged bedroom. She then dragged herself off the pod and onto the hygiene alcove for a quick wash. There were no showerheads in the Orange Creek. Instead, Euphrasia pushed a large bucket towards a faucet embedded into the center of the alcove, which let a metered amount of heated, fully recycled water pool into the bucket for her use.

After painstakingly washing herself with a water dipper without wasting so much as a single drop, Euphrasia dried herself off with a towel before fetching her clothes. As always, she began with her full-bodied black tunic, then her corset (or imitation of one). After checking herself in the mirror to affirm that her terrible sleeping habits hadn't ruined her looks yet, Euphrasia put on her gloves, her capelet, and her scarf next to fully cover every inch of her body in the dreary black that the El Howayecks were always known to wear.

[list]"Can't forget you of course," she muttered, last but not least grabbing her fur-lined hat that proudly ornamented in metal the Eye in Splendor. [/list]

Euphrasia stepped out of her bedroom and walked through the communal corridors of her apartment complex, her fellow residents bowing as they passed her by. She briefly considered stopping by the canteens to collect her share of the day, though the mushy, sometimes slimy burger patties never really inspired much confidence in her appetite. Instead, walking up a flight of stairs to the top of her apartment complex, she waited along the tracks for a maglev to take her to work. One arrives only seconds later, Euphrasia having perfectly predicted its arrival.

Easily finding a seat in the maglev (her fellow commuters immediately offering her their own), Euphrasia sighed and rested her head against the window before turning to stare at the landscape of the Orange Creek. She trailed her eyes at the horizon as the ground curved upwards into the sky, but there was no sky, instead an opposite strip of land dotted with inverted farms and habitats under the alternating bands of window panes that flooded the interior with mirrored sunlight.

Normally, any Erenite let alone Spacenoid used to the affairs of a celestial surface will be taken aback by the view of the Orange Creek, the disappearing horizon, the illusory daybreak that dimmed or brightened according to the demands of the population, the quiet transportation systems that broke the scenic greeneries, the vertical farms and vat-grown meat. But Euphrasia shook her head. The Orange Creek was a marvel, yes, but those that actually live within it understand that not everything is perfect.

Surrounded by beauty, you start to find other ugly things to whine about.

For one thing, she rolled her eyes as she looked up to the pale-faced man standing in front her seat. He raised one arm to grasp at the grab handles hanging overhead as the maglev began to move to its next stop. Turning to his side as the maglev began to move, the man raised the bangs of his blonde-white hair up and off his face, as if trying to get a better view of Euphrasia.

[list]"... Good morning, Gale..." Euphrasia says, looking away from the man, who grinned from ear to ear at the acknowledgement. "What's gotten you here this early?"

"Ms. Howayek! Didn't see ya there! The board increased how much feedback my sleeping pod gets," Gale said nonchalantly, "Said they were getting annoyed I kept sleeping in, so now they throw a damned earthquake whenever I wake up. Tough, ain't it?"

"Thankfully, I don't need someone else's prodding to get out of bed, being a grown adult and all. But hey, good for you."[/list]

Gale snickered, amused by the taunt. As the maglev made its next stop, he let go of the grab handles and sat down next to Euphrasia. On instinct, she immediately scooted away, not that Gale seemed to particularly care. He relaxed in his seat, spreading his arms wide over and letting the capelet of his grey tunic stretch open.

[list]"Today is a good day." Gale said, almost slumping down as he spoke. "Best day of my life, honestly."

"What makes you say that?" asked Euphrasia, clearly suspicious about the happiness of a war hawk.

"All days are great! But today though, heh... it's really such a wonderful thing to be rewarded for your efforts, wouldn't you agree?"

"Being a turncoat isn't a very taxing endeavor."

"Sure it is! Ever tried winning a feral cat's trust? Bloody Deliberators, man. You give them the whole world and they'll just nod quietly in response, no thank yous, no handshakes, like these things were expected from you. It's why I'm glad I'm finally with the good ones who know hard work when they come... though, I suppose Ms. Howayek has differing views?"

"Corporate responsibility includes trust, Gale. I wouldn't trust someone like you to burn in a firepit."

"Someone like me?"[/list]

The doors of the maglev swung open, and Euphrasia stepped out and onto the platform, cutting off the conversation with Gale who laughed and followed closely behind her. In front of Euphrasia was not a station, but a walkway that lead up into the front entrance of a great building. Well, the only great building anyways, what with the Orange Creek's strict laws on building heights and space. The façade was normally a whiteish grey typical of fiber reinforced concrete, but in the golden hour it illuminated beautifully like a royal chalice. 

If you didn't get a clue as to the building's importance that way, you'd certainly realize it once you stepped off the walkway look at the huge, onyx sign mounted on the garden display embedded into the staircase. On that sign, in unmistakable silver letters, were the words:

[list][list][list][list][list][list][list][list][b]11 LEAGUE PARK

OFFICIAL BUSINESS ONLY[/b][/list][/list][/list][/list][/list][/list][/list][/list]

Walk up the onyx black steps, and you are greeted by a large glass door, flanked on either side by armed units of the Orange Guard, who typically asked you for identification. Not Euphrasia though, and certainly not Gale, who would be permitted admission immediately. As a general rule to the commons, you never halt a corpo or a child thereof, for any good reason. Absolutely not if they were heading to 11 League Park, you'd be flogged for obstruction.

[list]"Listen, Ms. Howayek..." Gale began, matching Euphrasia's speedy, aversive gait, "Once all the fancy ceremonies are done and I get the nice handshake from His Majesty, I'll technically be outranking you..."

"What's your angle?" Euphrasia tersely responded, breezing past the central lobby and opening up one of the elevators, cringing as Gale entered too.

"It means you're gonna have to stop giving me the cold shoulder and accept reality, Ms. Howayek. The Rosenmarqet got what was coming to them, and so did those Deliberators. The fact that I can now happily stick myself into your pretty little morning routine means that the Board has given me their full confidence. If you keep stonewalling me, I can consider that an affront to corporate business, ya know?"

"Starting wars is bad business."

"Winning wars is not."

"So we won then?"

"Take a good look at me and say if you think I lost!"[/list]

Gale cackled, spreading open his arms dramatically like a blooming flower, seemingly more self-satisfied than he will ever be. Euphrasia turned away, uninterested in continuing the argument. Here she was, standing in an elevator with the man that had instigated everything, who was going so far as to gloat about it, and yet she couldn't do anything about it. 

Not yet anyways. The cameras in the elevator were rolling, as were the ones in the hallways, and all the way towards the shareholders' meeting room, but these cameras were owned by SummitONE. That's as good as them never having recorded anything to begin with.

A ping, and the elevator doors gently opened. Euphrasia stepped out and continued on her quiet way to the board meeting, Gale never once leaving her side until they were both in front of the two great maple doors of 11 League Park's main meeting room. Euphrasia turned to Gale one last time, squinting before turning to enter room.

The League of the Orange Creek was a very, very big corporation. Big corporations mean big boards of directors, and the League had 99. To accommodate that many directors at once, they couldn't just do the classical schtick of a gigantic table and a bunch of chairs all around. 

Instead, the League opted for this huge, insulated conference room, like a sort of indoor amphitheater for college plays or megachurch worships, with sleek black carpeting and slightly-less-sleek abstract artworks that hung from the walls to break the monotony of dark colors.

Of course, the sleekness of this room was immediately broken up by the vast multitude of executives that move to and fro all around. Some were sleeping in their chairs waiting for the meeting to begin, others were at the edge of the room next to the trays of free pastries and coffee eager to eat their money's worth for the transportation they did not pay for en route. 

There were a hundred single-seat sofas in the meeting room, neatly arranged in a 10x10 setup, interspersed between by small tables where executives could place their documents or food and drinks. They all pointed to the huge stage in front, and on that stage, a long table seating the senior-most officers of the board of directors. 

Euphemia, one of Euphrasia's two identical sisters, occupied the center of the table, happily chatting along with some of the directors on something menial. Note the spelling: Euphemia, Euphrasia. There was also another sister, Euphrosyne, though she hardly ever showed herself nowadays. Euphemia was identical to Euphrasia in every single way, since that's how identical siblings worked. And yet, people could spot the difference the two from a mile away, and it's not just because of Euphemia's lack of a hat or her ubiquitous use of an owl medallion pinned to her capelet, even just her behavior alone identified her.

[list]"Euphy!" she suddenly shouted out, waving enthusiastically to Euphrasia. "You're like, really late you know?!"

"Shut up Mia." Euphrasia immediately lambasted, tilting her hat downwards to avoid having to look at her sister's nosy friends. "I got here exactly on time anyways, what's the big deal?"
